mainTopic: Adding a month to the year (עיבור שנה) according to אחרים, and how many judges are needed for סמיכת זקנים and for giving סמיכה to a חכם.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion of עיבור שנה, adding a month to the year when the seasons fall behind. The גמרא explains that two earlier opinions differ over whether the day of the תקופה begins the new season or ends the old one. It then turns to אחרים, who add a month even when only fourteen days are missing. Two answers are given: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק says they are talking about ניסן and פסח, and רבינא says they mean סוכות, including the first יום טוב. The גמרא then moves to סמיכת זקנים, the elders leaning their hands on the communal bull. רבי יהודה counts five judges from the פסוק and רבי שמעון counts three, and the dispute rests on the word 'וסמכו' and a גזירה שוה from עולה. A ברייתא adds that giving סמיכה to a חכם also needs three. אביי finds no clear source for that number. רב אשי explains that this סמיכה is done by giving the title 'רבי' and the power to judge דיני קנסות. The amud ends with a challenge from the story of רבי יהודה בן בבא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The difference: does the season-change day begin or end a season?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers what the two earlier opinions disagree about. It is whether the day of the תקופה belongs to the new season or the old one, though we cannot tell which opinion holds which view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is whether the day of the תקופה starts the new season or finishes the old one. But we cannot tell which of them holds which view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question it was just asking: what is the real difference between the two earlier opinions? The answer is the status of the תקופה day itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The day the season changes could count as the first day of the new season (מתחיל) or the last day of the old one (גומר). That one-day difference explains why the two opinions give different numbers. The גמרא admits we know a disagreement exists but cannot match each view to its owner.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
The day the season changes (solstice or equinox)
Begins the new season / ends the old season
And they are not identified: we do not know who holds which view

steps.confusionAlert: Do not try to work out which opinion holds מתחיל and which holds גומר. The גמרא itself says this is not known.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם תְּקוּפָה מַתְחִיל וְיוֹם תְּקוּפָה גּוֹמֵר.
phrases.english: whether the day of the season-change begins the season, or the day of the season-change ends it.
But they are not identified.
phrases.notes: We know they argue about this, but not which one says which.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question about the difference between two opinions, asked before this section begins.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The disagreement is whether the תקופה day begins or ends a season, but the views are not assigned.

steps.title: אחרים: even fourteen days missing is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the view of אחרים from the ברייתא: the year is made longer even when only a small part of the month, fourteen days, is missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחרים say: we add a month even for a minority of the month. How much is a minority? Fourteen days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next opinion in the ברייתא, the view of אחרים, so that it can examine it. This is a setup for the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier opinions needed most of a month missing before making the year longer. אחרים are much stricter and say that even fourteen days, less than half a month, is enough. The obvious question is why so few days should matter.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others': a תנא quoted by this name
A minority of it, less than half the month
Adding a month to make a leap year

phrases.english: אחרים say: even for a minority of it.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the month: we add a month to the year when the season is short even by a minority of a month.

phrases.english: And how much is its minority? Fourteen days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אחרים, the year is made longer even when the season is only fourteen days short.

steps.title: Why should fourteen days matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what אחרים are thinking. If the תקופה day ends the old season, and we only need the whole festival in the new season, that condition is already met, so there is no reason to add a month.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do אחרים hold? If they hold that the תקופה day ends the season, and that we need the whole festival in the new season, that is already the case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אחרים. Under the usual assumptions, fourteen missing days still leave the festival in the new season, so why add a month?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that the festival must fall in the new season. Using the assumptions from the earlier discussion, the festival is already in the new season even with this shortfall. So the strict number of אחרים seems to have no reason behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they hold? What is their reasoning?
We need the entire festival to be in the new season
It is there: the condition is already met

phrases.english: What do they hold?
If they hold that the season-change day ends the season,
and that we need the whole festival in the new season, that is already there!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָסָבְרִי? אִי קָסָבְרִי יוֹם תְּקוּפָה גּוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the opinion of אחרים quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the standard assumptions, the festival is already in the new season, so the strict rule has no reason.

steps.title: אחרים are talking about ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק explains that אחרים are talking about the spring season of ניסן. The פסוק 'שמור את חדש האביב' teaches that the spring תקופה must fall within ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said: אחרים are talking about the season of ניסן, as it says 'Keep the month of spring.' Guard the spring season so that it is in the month of ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק answers the question by changing which season אחרים are discussing. They mean the spring season and ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the rule was only about the festival being in the new season. In ניסן there is a different requirement from the פסוק: the spring תקופה itself must fall in the month of ניסן, early enough, by the time of פסח. That stricter rule explains why fourteen days can matter.

keyTerms.meaning: They are 'standing in', meaning talking about
The spring season, which starts at the spring equinox
The month of spring

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the timing of פסח is tied to the spring season. That link is the main reason a leap year is ever needed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said:
אחרים are dealing with the season of ניסן,
as it is written: 'Keep the month of spring.'
Guard the spring of the season
so that it will be in the month of ניסן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the case: ניסן rather than the festival-only rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed אחרים only needed the festival to be in the new season.
steps.terutzMaskana: In ניסן the spring תקופה itself must fall within the month, early enough, which is a stricter rule.

steps.title: Why not just add a day to אדר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the problem is only a few days, just make אדר one day longer instead of adding a whole month.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them just lengthen אדר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 4. A small shortfall could be fixed by making אדר longer, without adding a whole month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding one day to אדר pushes all the dates in ניסן back by a day. That might be enough to bring the תקופה into the right part of ניסן. So adding a full month seems like too much.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them make אדר longer by adding a day

phrases.english: But let them lengthen אדר!
phrases.notes: Here 'lengthen' means making אדר a 30-day month by adding one day, not adding a whole month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ניסן answer given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק's explanation that אחרים are discussing ניסן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Adding one day to אדר could solve a borderline case, so there is no need for a leap year.

steps.title: The תנא was counting downward
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב explains that אחרים counted from the large shortfalls downward. We make the year longer for any shortfall down to fourteen days, but at fourteen itself we do not, and adding a day to אדר is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: the תנא counted from the top down. He means: we make the year longer down to the minority. How much is the minority? Fourteen days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב answers the question about אדר. He rereads 'fourteen days' as the lower limit where adding a month stops, not the point where it starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge read אחרים as saying 'at fourteen days, add a month.' רב אחא בר יעקב reads it as 'add a month for bigger shortfalls, down to fourteen.' At fourteen itself, adding one day to אדר works, so the challenge is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: He is counting from the top down
Up to, but not including
We make the year longer by adding a month

steps.confusionAlert: 'Down to fourteen' does not include fourteen. At exactly fourteen days we do not add a month.

phrases.english: רב אחא בר יעקב said:
The תנא is counting from the top downward,
phrases.notes: He starts from the big numbers of missing days and counts down.

phrases.english: and this is what he means: we add a month down to the minority.
And how much is the minority? Fourteen days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about אדר in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Fourteen days' was the point at which a month is added.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fourteen is the lower limit. We add a month only for larger shortfalls, and at fourteen a day is added to אדר instead.

steps.title: רבינא: אחרים are talking about תשרי and סוכות
steps.stepSummary: רבינא gives a different answer to step 3. אחרים are talking about תשרי, and they need the whole חג, including the first יום טוב, to fall in the new season.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: really, אחרים are talking about תשרי. They hold that we need the whole festival in the new season, even the first יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the original question from step 3 in a new way. He keeps the case in תשרי but adds a stricter requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that 'the whole festival' did not have to include the first day. רבינא says אחרים count even the first יום טוב of סוכות, so the new season must begin before it. That is why a shortfall of fourteen days matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth: going back to the original approach
The autumn month in which סוכות falls
The first festival day of סוכות

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for אחרים. Either they mean ניסן, as רב שמואל בר רב יצחק says, or they mean תשרי with the first יום טוב included, as רבינא says.

phrases.english: רבינא said:
Really, אחרים are dealing with תשרי,
and אחרים hold that we need the whole festival in the new season,
including the first יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם אֲחֵרִים בְּתִשְׁרִי קָיְימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the challenge in step 3, in place of רב שמואל בר רב יצחק's answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'The whole festival' did not include the first יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: For אחרים, even the first יום טוב of סוכות must be in the new season.

steps.title: But the פסוק calls it 'חג האסיף'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבינא: the תורה calls סוכות 'the festival of gathering,' and crops cannot be gathered on יום טוב. So it seems the first day should not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first יום טוב? It is written 'the festival of gathering'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבינא's claim that the first יום טוב must be in the new season, using the name the פסוק gives the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'חג האסיף' sounds like the days when gathering happens. Gathering is forbidden on יום טוב, so the name seems to describe only חול המועד. That would leave the first day out of 'the festival.'

keyTerms.meaning: The festival of gathering the crops: a name for סוכות
It is written

phrases.english: The first יום טוב?
It is written: 'The festival of gathering'!
phrases.notes: שמות 23:16. You cannot gather crops on יום טוב, so the name seems to point to חול המועד.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן? חַג הָאָסִיף כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's answer in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: Including the first יום טוב in the requirement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Festival of gathering' seems to mean only days when gathering is allowed, which leaves out the first יום טוב.

steps.title: It means the festival that comes in gathering season
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'חג האסיף' means the festival that falls in the season of gathering. It is not limited to the days when gathering actually happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means the festival that comes at the time of gathering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the פסוק differently. The name describes the season, not the specific days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Gathering' describes the time of year when סוכות falls, which is autumn. So the name does not leave out the first יום טוב, and רבינא's explanation stands.

keyTerms.meaning: In the season of gathering crops

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבינא, אחרים require all of סוכות, from the first יום טוב on, to fall in the new season. This is why a fourteen-day shortfall is enough to add a month.

phrases.english: The festival that comes in the season of gathering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'חג האסיף' refers only to days when gathering is allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'חג האסיף' names the season of the festival, so the first יום טוב is included.

steps.title: Who are the elders? Not just anyone in the marketplace
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next item, סמיכת זקנים, and brings a ברייתא. It shows that the 'elders' who lay hands are not ordinary old people but leaders of the עדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the laying of hands by the elders. The רבנן taught: 'And the elders shall lay.' You might think this means any elders in the marketplace. So the פסוק says 'of the congregation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new item from the משנה, סמיכת זקנים, and starts a ברייתא that defines who the 'elders' are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'זקני' alone could mean any older person. The added word 'עדה' limits it to people who lead and judge the community. This is the first step in narrowing down who must do the סמיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The elders leaning their hands on the communal bull-offering
The Rabbis taught (this opens a ברייתא)
Elders of the marketplace, meaning ordinary old people with no court position
The פסוק teaches us (by saying a specific word)
Congregation; here it refers to the leaders and judges of the people

phrases.english: The laying of hands by the elders.
The Rabbis taught:
"And the elders shall lay"
You might think this means elders of the marketplace?
So the verse says "congregation."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of עיבור השנה (steps 1–9) and begins the next item of the משנה, סמיכת זקנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The elders who perform סמיכה must be leaders of the עדה, not ordinary elders.

steps.title: Not the smaller courts, but the special ones of the congregation
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא narrows further. 'עדה' alone might include the smaller courts, but 'העדה' with the extra letter ה points to the special members, the great סנהדרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it only said 'congregation,' you might think even the lesser ones of the congregation count. So the פסוק says 'THE congregation,' meaning the special ones of the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes one step further and shows that only the most important judges, members of the great סנהדרין, can do this סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra letter ה, 'THE congregation,' is read as pointing to the special, best-known part of the עדה. This rules out the smaller courts (סנהדרי קטנה) and leaves the great סנהדרין.

keyTerms.meaning: The lesser ones of the congregation, meaning the smaller courts
THE congregation; the extra ה points to its special members
The special ones of the congregation, meaning the great סנהדרין

phrases.english: If it only said "congregation,"
you might think it means the lesser ones of the congregation?
So the verse says "THE congregation":
the special ones of the congregation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and narrows the group further than step 10 did.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סמיכה must be done by members of the great סנהדרין.

steps.title: How many judges? רבי יהודה says five
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how many elders are needed. רבי יהודה counts 'וסמכו' as two and 'זקני' as two, then adds one because a court cannot be even, for a total of five.
steps.simpleTranslation: How many must there be? 'Shall lay' (plural) means two. 'Elders' (plural) means two more. A court cannot have an even number, so we add one more. That makes five. This is רבי יהודה's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now asks how many judges are needed, and רבי יהודה works it out from the words of the פסוק to get five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every plural word counts as at least two. רבי יהודה counts two plural words, so he gets four. Since a בית דין may not be an even number, he adds one more and reaches five.

keyTerms.meaning: And how many are they?
A court with an even number of judges, which is not allowed
We add one more to them
The תנא who holds that five judges are needed

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think five means five separate פסוקים. It is all one פסוק: two plural words give four, and one more is added only so the court is not even.

phrases.english: And how many are they?
"Shall lay" means two,
phrases.notes: The word is plural, and a plural means at least two.

phrases.english: "elders" means two,
and a court may not be an even number,
so we add one more to them,
so here there are five.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After saying WHO does the סמיכה, the ברייתא now asks HOW MANY.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, five judges perform סמיכת זקנים.

steps.title: רבי שמעון says three
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון counts only the word 'זקני' as two, adds one so the court is not even, and gets three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: 'Elders' means two. A court cannot be even, so we add one more. That makes three.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with רבי יהודה and counts only one plural word, so he needs only three judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole difference is the word 'וסמכו.' רבי יהודה counts it and רבי שמעון does not. The rest of the גמרא explains why each one reads that word his way.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who holds that three judges are needed
Three

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: five (counts 'וסמכו' and 'זקני'). רבי שמעון: three (counts only 'זקני'). Both add one so the court is not even.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
"Elders" means two,
and a court may not be an even number,
so we add one more to them,
so here there are three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יהודה's count of five.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, three judges perform סמיכת זקנים.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי שמעון count 'וסמכו'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון: the plural word 'וסמכו' is right there in the פסוק, so why doesn't he count it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון? Isn't it written 'And they shall lay'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks רבי שמעון why he ignores the plural word 'וסמכו', which should add two more judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that a plural word teaches 'two.' So the question is why רבי שמעון treats 'זקני' as a plural that counts but leaves out 'וסמכו', which is just as plural.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written...?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon,
isn't it written "And they shall lay"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבי שמעון's count in step 13 by using רבי יהודה's reading from step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'וסמכו' is plural, so by the same method it should add two judges.

steps.title: 'וסמכו' is needed for the act itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers for רבי שמעון: 'וסמכו' is needed to teach the act itself, that the elders must lay their hands. So it is not free to teach a number.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is needed for itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי שמעון: the word 'וסמכו' is busy teaching that there is a סמיכה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word that is needed for its plain meaning cannot also be used to count judges. For רבי שמעון, without 'וסמכו' we would not know the elders must lay their hands, so it teaches only that.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for something else)
For itself, for its own plain meaning

phrases.english: That word is needed for itself.
phrases.notes: He means it teaches the basic act: the elders must lay their hands on the bull.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The word is used up by its plain meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'וסמכו' is plural and should add two judges.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון, 'וסמכו' teaches that the סמיכה must happen, not how many do it.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the פסוק could have taught the act without 'וסמכו'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rejects the idea that 'וסמכו' is needed for itself. The פסוק could have said 'the elders of the congregation, their hands on the head of the bull,' and we would still know about the act.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? It is not needed for itself. If 'And they shall lay' did not come to teach something extra, let the פסוק write: 'the elders of the congregation, their hands on the head of the bull.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהודה's reply: 'וסמכו' is not needed to teach the act, so it is free to count two more judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה argues that the act of סמיכה would be clear from the words 'their hands on the head of the bull' even without the verb. Since the פסוק added the verb 'וסמכו' anyway, it must be there to teach something extra, the number of judges.

keyTerms.meaning: Is not needed
For an extra teaching drawn from the word
Let it write (the פסוק could have written)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda, what does he say?
It is not needed for itself,
because if "And they shall lay" did not come to teach something extra,
let it write: "The elders of the congregation,
their hands on the head of the bull."
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק with the verb taken out, and the act would still be clear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 15 from רבי יהודה's side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that 'וסמכו' is needed for its plain meaning
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The act would be clear even without the verb, so the verb is extra and can be used for counting.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: without 'וסמכו' we might think 'next to' the head
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers: without the verb, the word 'על' could mean 'next to' the head. So 'וסמכו' is needed to show the hands go right on the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון? If it were written that way, I would have said: what does 'on' mean? Next to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי שמעון again: without 'וסמכו,' we might think the elders only put their hands near the bull's head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'על' can mean 'on' or 'next to.' For רבי שמעון, the verb 'וסמכו' (lean) shows that the hands must actually press on the head. So the verb is still needed for itself and cannot count judges.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought
On; it can also mean next to
Next to, nearby

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon:
if it were written that way,
I would have said:
What does "on" mean? Next to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, אִי כְּתִיב הָכִי, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהודה's argument in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the word is still needed to block a wrong reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without 'וסמכו,' 'על' could mean the hands are only next to the head.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וסמכו' teaches that the hands must go directly on the head, so it is used up.

steps.title: רבי יהודה learns 'directly on the head' from עולה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says we already know the hands go right on the head from a גזירה שוה with עולה, where the word 'ראש' also appears. So 'וסמכו' is still free to count judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה learns 'head' 'head' from the burnt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהודה's reply: we learn that the hands go on the head itself from the עולה, not from 'וסמכו.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the עולה, the hands are placed right on the animal's head. Since both פסוקים use the word 'ראש,' רבי יהודה applies the same rule here through a גזירה שוה. So he does not need 'וסמכו' to block the 'next to' reading.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns (one case from another)
'Head' and 'head', the same word in two פסוקים, which links them in a גזירה שוה
Burnt-offering

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda
learns "head" "head" from the burnt-offering.
phrases.notes: See ויקרא 1:4, where by the עולה the hand is placed on its head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי שמעון's 'next to' concern from step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Another source covers the point, so the word stays free
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'וסמכו' is needed to show the hands go right on the head.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה from עולה already teaches this, so 'וסמכו' can count two judges.

steps.title: רבי שמעון does not accept the גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: The argument ends: רבי שמעון does not learn 'ראש' 'ראש' from עולה. So for him 'וסמכו' is still needed for itself, and he stays with three judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון does not learn 'head' 'head' from the burnt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the back-and-forth: the whole dispute comes down to whether we accept the גזירה שוה from עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the גזירה שוה, רבי שמעון needs 'וסמכו' to teach that the hands go right on the head. So it cannot add judges, and he counts only 'זקני' for three. רבי יהודה accepts the גזירה שוה, so 'וסמכו' is free and he counts five.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not learn (does not accept this link)

steps.whatToRemember: The five-or-three dispute rests on one word, 'וסמכו.' רבי יהודה learns 'directly on the head' from עולה, so 'וסמכו' adds two judges (five). רבי שמעון does not, so 'וסמכו' is needed for the act itself (three).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon
does not learn "head" "head" from the burnt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי שמעון's final reply to step 18 and closes the dispute.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute between five and three judges depends on whether one accepts the גזירה שוה 'ראש' 'ראש' from עולה.

steps.title: A ברייתא: both kinds of laying hands need three
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that סמיכה and סמיכת זקנים are both done with three judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: laying hands, and laying hands of the elders, are done with three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that names two kinds of 'laying hands' and says both need three judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that the elders lay their hands on the פר העלם דבר, and that for רבי שמעון this takes three. This ברייתא lists a second kind of סמיכה next to that one, and it does not yet say what the second kind is.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught (a ברייתא is being quoted)
Laying hands
Laying hands of the elders
With three (judges)

phrases.english: It was taught: laying hands and laying hands of the elders are with three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that connects to רבי שמעון's count of three elders (steps 13-19) and adds a second kind of סמיכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both types of סמיכה require three judges.

steps.title: What are the two kinds of סמיכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what each of the two terms in the ברייתא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'laying hands' and what is 'laying hands of the elders'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the two names in the ברייתא refer to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One kind is clearly the elders laying hands on the פר העלם דבר. The question is what the other kind is, since the ברייתא lists them as two separate things.

keyTerms.meaning: What is

phrases.english: What is 'laying hands' and what is 'laying hands of the elders'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the terms in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the second kind of סמיכה in the ברייתא refers to.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: it means giving סמיכה to a חכם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that one of the terms means giving סמיכה to elders.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: it means giving סמיכה to elders.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that the second kind of סמיכה is giving סמיכה to a חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the ברייתא is teaching two different laws. Laying hands on the פר needs three, and appointing a חכם with סמיכה also needs three.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving סמיכה to elders, appointing them as ordained חכמים

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Giving סמיכה to elders.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second kind of סמיכה is giving סמיכה to חכמים.

steps.title: אביי asks: where do we learn that giving סמיכה needs three?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף for the source that giving סמיכה to a חכם needs three judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: from where do we know that giving סמיכה to elders is done with three?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks for a source in the תורה for the rule that giving סמיכה to a חכם needs three judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the פר, the number came from words in the פסוק, as we saw earlier. For giving סמיכה to a חכם, אביי wants to know what the source is.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it?

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
Giving סמיכה to elders with three, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source of the rule that was just explained.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the תורה for needing three judges to give סמיכה.

steps.title: משה gave סמיכה alone, so one should be enough
steps.stepSummary: If the source is משה giving סמיכה to יהושע, that would show that one person is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it comes from the פסוק 'and he laid his hands on him', then one person should be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי suggests a possible source, the story of משה and יהושע, and shows right away that it proves the wrong number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה gave סמיכה to יהושע by himself. If that story is our model, it would teach that one person is enough, not three.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say
If so
One should be enough

phrases.english: If you say it is from what is written:
'And he laid his hands on him,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:23, where משה gives סמיכה to יהושע.

phrases.english: If so, one should be enough!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִדִּכְתִיב וַיִּסְמֹךְ אֶת יָדָיו עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests a source for step 23 and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using משה's סמיכה of יהושע as the source for needing three.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In that story only one person gave סמיכה, so it would teach one, not three.

steps.title: Maybe משה counts as seventy-one
steps.stepSummary: A suggested defense: משה was not like one ordinary judge. He stood in place of the whole סנהדרין of seventy-one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: משה stood in place of seventy-one,
steps.whatsHappening: אביי, still speaking to רב יוסף, suggests a way to save the source: משה was equal to a full סנהדרין, so the story does not prove that one ordinary person is enough. He rejects this in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer explains why משה could give סמיכה alone. His single act is treated as the act of seventy-one judges.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say
Seventy-one, the number of the great סנהדרין

phrases.english: And if you say:
Moses stood in place of seventy-one,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא מֹשֶׁה בִּמְקוֹם שִׁבְעִים וְחַד קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: משה's single act counts as a full court.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה's story shows that one person is enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: משה was equal to seventy-one, so his story does not teach that one is enough.

steps.title: Then we would need seventy-one
steps.stepSummary: The suggested defense fails: if משה stood for seventy-one, then every סמיכה should need seventy-one judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should need seventy-one!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects the answer of step 25, because it proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If משה is our model and he counted as seventy-one, then the rule should be seventy-one judges, not three. Either way, this story does not give us the number three.

keyTerms.meaning: It should require

phrases.english: If so, it should require seventy-one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense of step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole idea of using משה as the source for three.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The idea leads to seventy-one judges, not three.

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends this search with 'קשיא': no clear source for three is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that it cannot find a source in the פסוקים for needing three judges to give סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of the ברייתא stays in place. The only thing left without an answer is where the number three comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult (the question stays without an answer)

steps.whatToRemember: Giving סמיכה to a חכם needs three, but the גמרא could not find a source in the פסוקים for that number.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'קשיא' does not cancel the rule. It only means the source is still unknown, and the הלכה of three stays.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes אביי's search for a source.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no clear source for three, but the rule of three stays.

steps.title: Is סמיכה really done with the hands?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי whether they actually put their hands on the person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: do they really lay their hands on him?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins about how giving סמיכה to a חכם is actually done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the פר, the elders really put their hands on its head. The question is whether giving סמיכה to a חכם also means placing hands on him, the way משה did with יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: Really with the hand
They give him סמיכה

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
Do they give him סמיכה really with the hand?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the number of judges to how the act is done.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether giving סמיכה to a חכם is a physical act with the hands.

steps.title: סמיכה is done by giving a title and authority
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that סמיכה is done with words: they call him 'רבי' and give him the right to judge דיני קנסות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: they give him סמיכה with a name. They call him 'רבי' and give him permission to judge cases of fines.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains that this סמיכה is not done with the hands. It is done by giving the person a title and legal authority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving סמיכה is a formal appointment. The person gets the title 'רבי' and the power to judge דיני קנסות, which only judges with סמיכה can do.

keyTerms.meaning: With a name or title
Permission, authority
Cases of fines set by the תורה

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows what סמיכה really gives a חכם: the power to judge דיני קנסות. That is why the next steps worry that these laws could be forgotten.

phrases.english: He said to him:
They give him סמיכה with a name,
They call him 'Rabbi,'
And they give him permission
To judge cases of fines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סמיכה means giving the title 'רבי' and the authority to judge דיני קנסות, not placing hands.

steps.title: Can't one person give סמיכה? The praise of רבי יהודה בן בבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule of three by quoting רב's praise of רבי יהודה בן בבא, who saved דיני קנסות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one person cannot give סמיכה? But רב יהודה said in the name of רב: that man should be remembered for good, and רבי יהודה בן בבא is his name, because if not for him, דיני קנסות would have been forgotten from ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge against the rule that three are needed. It quotes רב's praise of רבי יהודה בן בבא, and the full proof will come as the story continues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether one person alone might be able to give סמיכה. The quote suggests that רבי יהודה בן בבא did something by himself that saved these laws. The details of what he did come in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say?
Indeed, however
Remembered for good
If not for

phrases.english: And one person cannot give סמיכה?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say that Rav said:
Indeed, that man is remembered for good,
And Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava is his name,
For if not for him,
The laws of fines would have been forgotten from Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד לָא סָמֵיךְ? וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's rule of three, using רב's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that giving סמיכה needs three judges.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's statement points to a time when one person alone gave סמיכה and so saved דיני קנסות.

steps.title: Why would the laws be forgotten? Just learn them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רב's wording: laws can be kept by studying them, so how would they be forgotten?
steps.simpleTranslation: Would they be forgotten? Let them learn them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to question רב's words. Laws do not disappear if people keep learning them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowledge can be kept alive through learning, so 'forgotten' cannot mean that people would no longer know these laws. This forces a new reading of what רב meant.

keyTerms.meaning: They would be forgotten
Let them learn them

phrases.english: Would they be forgotten? Let them learn them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the statement quoted in step 30.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Laws that can be studied cannot really be forgotten.

steps.title: The גמרא starts to explain what רב meant
steps.stepSummary: With 'אלא', the גמרא begins to explain רב's words in a new way. The explanation continues in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer to step 31. The word 'אלא' (rather) begins a new explanation of what רב meant, and the rest comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אלא' means the plain reading is being set aside. The new explanation, which follows, will tell us what was really at risk of being lost.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a new explanation)

phrases.english: Rather,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question of step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading רב's words (the explanation continues next).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Forgotten' means people would no longer know these laws.
steps.terutzMaskana: A different meaning, which the גמרא gives next.
